exposure: Congenital uterine anomalies (septate uterus, arcuate uterus, unicornuate uterus, bicornuate uterus)
cohort: The study included 460 cesarean section patients from KIMS & RF, Amalapuram, between February 2023 and January 2024, among whom 14 (3.04%) were diagnosed with uterine anomalies during surgery.
finding: Uterine anomalies in cesarean section patients were associated with a high incidence of low birth weight, preterm delivery, malpresentation, and intrauterine growth restriction, though the majority of neonates had satisfactory Apgar scores.
